original.target_description: Unassigned original-side placeholder; original source was not inspected.

replication.target_description: Located female-identified undergraduate profiles, comparisons of profile indicators, PTSS, and total CU/overall maltreatment; exact target comparison unresolved from supplied description and p. 13 locator.

n.sample_role: Candidate counts are female-identified undergraduate participants in mutually exclusive LPA profiles; target-test analytic sample unresolved.
n.exclusions: Recruitment 724; excluded invalid responding n = 157, age >24 n = 17, gender other/nonresponse n = 4; final overall sample 546. PTSS missing for 37 males and 43 females without an endorsed traumatic event. Exclusion counts are source-reported, not allocated to gender.
n.location: Table 2, p. 901 (PDF p. 14); Methods p. 894; analytic plan/results pp. 896–899; Table 1 p. 897

reported_success.quote:
Regarding differences in child maltreatment experiences, neglect was higher
in the secondary CU group compared to the primary CU group for both males
and females. This is inconsistent with one previous study (Kimonis et al.,
2013b) finding neglect experiences were highest in the primary CU group and
early theory ... As far as
we know, studies have not examined whether CU trait variants within a female
population differ based on CU facets. This preliminary examination suggests
further explorations may be necessary to better understand how CU traits
manifest in female samples when considering variant groups. ... For both males and females, PTSS were highest in the
secondary CU groups consistent with past research (e.g., Sharf et al., 2014).

notes: Only n_r and reported_success assigned; original and replication es/p are unassigned placeholders. Target identification uses explicit gender labels, not row order or numeric matching. The gender identifies the sample, but the description "Comparison of adolescents' scores on measured variables" and locator p. 13 do not identify a unique outcome/test. PDF p. 13 is Discussion, printed p. 900. The paper reports separate MANOVAs for profile indicators, PTSS, and total CU/overall maltreatment, plus pairwise comparisons. Final-profile counts are candidates only; PTSS has additional missingness. Female counts also differ between Tables 1 and 2. No global target match or analytic N is asserted. Candidate final-profile participant count only: 60 + 32 + 14 + 197 = 303. Groups are mutually exclusive female LPA profiles in Table 2 and Results p. 896; this is not established as the analytic N of the unspecified critical comparison. Table 1 instead prints female group counts 55 + 25 + 12 + 168 = 260; source does not reconcile this discrepancy. PTSD symptoms are missing for 43 females; no test N was calculated by subtraction or from df. Female CU-facet comparison is presented as preliminary with no known prior female-variant facet studies; neglect findings are explicitly inconsistent with Kimonis et al. (2013b); PTSS findings are consistent with past research. These are separate outcome-specific narratives. Candidate tests retained without selecting: first MANOVA compares nine clustering indicators (p. 898); second compares PTSS (p. 899); third compares total CU and overall maltreatment (p. 899); Table 3 also gives pairwise superscripts. No effect size or p extracted because neither is assigned. PDF pages 10 and 13–16 were rendered and visually inspected, confirming the conflicting female Table 1/Table 2 counts and discussion/table layout.
